title: On-call handoff notes — Samir Ali (2026-03-03)
content:
Shift date: 2026-03-03
Owner: Samir Ali
Shift window: 20:00 PST - 08:00 PST (overnight)

Summary:
- Night saw repeated tail-latency spikes for hosted-api route /v1/generate between ~22:15-23:05 PST. Impact: increased 95th/99th token latency and several API timeouts for a small percentage of requests (~0.3%).
- Root cause (current hypothesis): intermittent DB connection flaps to kv-cache layer (redis cluster) causing cache misses and higher GPU work per request. Likely related to recent redis patch rollout on infra nodes.
- Major mitigations applied: scaled dedicated pool + rolled restart of redis pods in us-west-2; forced route fallback to smaller model variant (gpt-small-1) for non-SLA traffic to reduce load while restarts completed.

Incidents & timeline:
- 22:12 PST: PagerDuty alert P12345 triggered for increased 95th latency on hosted-api-prod.
- 22:18 PST: Notified infra oncall (Lexi) and started checking kv-cache metrics (db error rate spiked).
- 22:22 PST: Scaled up redis replica count from 3->5 (temporary) via infra autoscale; started rolling restart of redis nodes with zero-downtime flag.
- 22:30 PST: Applied routing change to route non-SLA tier to gpt-small-1 using redwoodctl (see commands below). This reduced GPU pressure.
- 22:45 PST: Latency returned close to baseline; monitoring shows error rate reduced.
- 23:05 PST: All restarts completed; rolled back temp scaling to 3 replicas at 23:20 PST after stabilization.

Temporary procedures performed (notes for runbook):
- When kv-cache error-rate > 1% and latency > SLO threshold, do the following in order:
  1) Notify infra oncall and add to incident channel #sre-oncall.
  2) Check redis cluster health: kubectl get pods -n infra | grep redis
  3) If errors show OOM or connection refusals, trigger rolling restart: kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis -n infra --grace-period=60
  4) Scale replicas up by +2 (kubectl scale statefulset/redis --replicas=5) if cluster CPU > 70% and error rate > 1%.
  5) Apply routing fallback for non-SLA traffic: redwoodctl routes set-fallback --route hosted-api-prod --policy model_variant=gpt-small-1 --priority temporary --reason "kv-cache degradation"
  6) Monitor token latency (redwood metrics: hosted_api_latency_p95) and error rate for next 30 minutes.
- Roll back fallback only after 30m of stable metrics and infra confirms redis cluster is healthy.

Commands used (examples):
- Check redis pods: kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=redis
- Rolling restart redis: kubectl rollout restart statefulset/redis -n infra --grace-period=60
- Scale redis replicas: kubectl scale statefulset/redis redis --replicas=5 -n infra
- Apply temporary model fallback: redwoodctl routes set-fallback --route hosted-api-prod --policy model_variant=gpt-small-1 --duration 2h --note "temp fallback during kv-cache incident"
- Rollback: redwoodctl routes remove-fallback --route hosted-api-prod --id <fallback-id>

Open follow-ups (create tickets):
- INFRA-549: Investigate root cause of redis connection flaps after patch; include kernel/connlimit checks. Assigned to infra team (Lexi).
- INFRA-550: Add health-check to prevent OOM-caused restarts from cycling into failure loop (suggest longer graceful period). Assigned: platform-eng.
- SRE-234: Formalize runbook steps above into Confluence and add step-by-step screenshots for using redwoodctl.

Runbook draft sections to add (TODO):
- Add quick-check dashboard panels (p95, p99, redis error-rate, gpu-utilization) and links.
- Add exact PagerDuty escalation tree with phone/pager ids (redact in public runbook).
- Add automated playbook to perform fallback via API when metrics cross threshold (to reduce manual steps).

Escalation contacts (oncall):
- Primary infra oncall: Lexi Martin (Slack: @lexi)
- Secondary infra eng: Jamie Chen (Slack: @jamie)
- SRE lead: Priya Kaur (Slack: @priya)
- Product ops (for customer comms): Alex Gomez (Slack: @alexg)

Notes to next shift:
- Keep an eye on redis error-rate for next 24 hours; infra rolled back the patch but flagged as potentially unstable.
- If repeat occurrences happen, do NOT scale down replicas below 3 until infra confirms fix.
- If latency spikes recur, apply same temporary fallback but extend duration to 4h and notify product ops before public incident comms.

Misc scratchpad / links:
- Incident dashboard: https://app.datadog.com/dash/12345/hosted-api-latency
- Confluence runbook draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SRE/pages/123456789/Oncall+Runbooks
- GitHub infra PR related to redis patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/321
- Jira tickets: INFRA-542 (initial alert), INFRA-549 (follow-up)

End of shift handoff. Leaving this as a working draft — please add edits directly in Confluence and ping me on Slack if anything ambiguous.

- Samir
